transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2026-05-06 11:30 PDT | Duration: 52m | Recording: Auto
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Linus Park (Redwood SE), Tom Reed (Redwood Partnerships), Sam Ortega (Lighthouse Head of Platform), Maya Chen (Lighthouse Cloud Eng), Diego Alvarez (Lighthouse Security), Rina Patel (Product)

Auto Summary: Quick preflight to align on listing requirements and network connectivity for edge GKE clusters. Main asks: VPC peering pattern that works with Lighthouse's NAT/proxying, KMS integration questions for encrypted keys, and a throughput run with a quantized model on their A10-class nodes.

[00:00] Jordan: Alright hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick roll call then we'll dive into the network diagram you sent, thanks Maya.
[00:18] Sam: Yeah thanks, um we wanted to make sure we don't block the marketplace listing and also want to validate the connectivity pattern to our edge clusters. We're running GKE anthos-ish clusters at remote sites that sit behind a central NAT.
[00:32] Priya: Got it, thumbs up. Can you confirm whether each edge site has a routable CIDR or is it all hairpinned through a single egress?
[00:44] Maya: Right now it's single egress per region, so site traffic goes out via a central kube-proxy NAT; we don't have unique public IP per site.
[00:55] Linus: That makes sense, so our typical patterns would be either: 1) VPC peering from Redwood Private control plane into your central VPC and then route to sites, or 2) a reverse-proxy (we call connector) initiated outbound to Redwood, TLS over TCP, which avoids peering but needs persistent outbound.
[01:16] Sam: Hmm okay the peering option is probably cleaner for latency, but we have restrictions on peering across accounts for compliance, it's messy.
[01:26] Diego: From security side we prefer outbound-only connections, less surface area, but curious how Redwood handles auth and mTLS.
[01:35] Priya: For outbound connectors we use a short-lived certificate issued by Redwood's control plane, with mutual TLS. The connector establishes an encrypted tunnel and we maintain a small NAT hole. We can also optionally integrate KMS for key sealing.
[01:53] Maya: Is that compatible with our HSM? We have an on-prem HSM for key custody, FIPS mode.
[02:02] Linus: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and some customers plug in HSM-backed KMS via our private deployment. There can be an extra step for key rotation and attestation but it's supported.
[02:20] Sam: Cool. One of our questions: marketplace listing demands a packaged deployment artifact for both hosted and dedicated patterns — what exactly do you need from us?
[02:33] Jordan: From the marketplace side we need a short deployment doc, an architecture diagram, and confirmation of support boundaries. For listing we also need billing metering hooks and an owner point of contact. We'll send a checklist after this call.
[02:46] Rina: On billing, do we need any special telemetry in the edge agent to report token counts? Our current metric set is requests/sec and CPU.
[02:58] Priya: For accurate per-token billing, Redwood's SDK can emit token deltas; on private deployments we can also aggregate at the gateway. If you prefer not to change edge agent we can do metering at the control plane level as long as there's a stable correlation. There's some small error but it's workable.
[03:18] Maya: Okay that sounds doable.
[03:20] [03:21] Tom: Quick interruption — competitors asked about integrated billing in prior deals, how do you handle invoicing?
[03:28] Jordan: For marketplace listing we usually support a reseller flow or direct invoicing; for pilots it's common to do credit-backed usage. We'll include options in the checklist.
[03:36] [03:40] Sam: Let's talk about the benchmark. We want a short run to judge latency and token cost. Our infra team uses A10 GPUs at the edge, usually two GPUs per site.
[03:52] Priya: We're proposing a micro-benchmark: 1) quantized 4-bit LLM (we'll suggest a model), 2) run 10k token mixed prompts across a small pool (2 instances) for 15 minutes, capture tail latency and tokens/sec. We can run this on your A10 fleet or provide a Redwood Dedicated trial instance.
[04:16] Maya: Could you clarify what you mean by 'quantized' — will that affect quality vs cost?
[04:22] Linus: Yes quantization reduces memory and compute per token; typical 4-bit configs give 10-30% quality delta on some tasks but huge throughput wins. We'll share recommended quant profiles per workload.
[04:37] Diego: On security we need to see encryption in transit + at rest, audit logs, and SSO integration. Do you have SOC2 or ISO certs?
[04:46] Jordan: Redwood has SOC2 Type II in our hosted offering. For private deployments, audit logging and KMS/HSM integration are in scope — we'll share our security pack.
[04:56] Rina: Any gotchas with key rotation frequency? Our security policy mandates rotation every 90 days.
[05:03] Linus: We support automatic rotation via KMS, and customer-managed key rotations can be scheduled; rotation windows might cause short re-keying delays if a live cache needs to be invalidated — we can walk you through a zero-downtime rotation flow.
[05:22] [05:25] Sam: Regarding network, one detail: our site egress IPs are ephemeral. If Redwood expects static NAT IPs for allowlisting that could be a problem.
[05:35] Priya: For allowlisting we can support two modes: static IP ranges from Redwood Dedicated or connector mode where you don't have to open inbound ports. Connector mode avoids allowlisting.
[05:47] Maya: Connector mode's the preferred path. What's the persistent connection behavior? Idle timeouts?
[05:53] Linus: Idle connections will be kept alive but we have reconnection backoff and a quick start path; average recon time is sub-2s in normal conditions. Still if sites are very flaky we'll recommend a local cache + fallback model variant to avoid tail latency spikes.
[06:12] Jordan: Also, for marketplace listing we need a short SLA statement for the listing page. Do you already have internal uptime targets for edge features?
[06:21] Sam: We commit to 99.5% for core services, edge availability tends to be lower. We'll mark that in the listing but want to understand Redwood's fallback options.
[06:30] Priya: Redwood's routing policy can automatically fallback to a hosted model variant if private connectivity fails, preserving availability but with higher cost and possibly different latency. That's a supported pattern.
[06:44] [07:00] Maya: On observability — what hooks do you provide? We need traces, per-request IDs, and token-level timing if possible.
[07:09] Linus: We emit request IDs, model-level traces, and latency histograms. Token-level timing is heavier but available in debug mode. For marketplace customers we can surface a trimmed set of dashboards.
[07:28] Jordan: I'll attach a sample dashboard to the checklist.
[07:31] [08:10] Sam: A couple of gotchas from procurement: we need a way to sign the marketplace contract via SSO and some vendors insist on anchor-of-trust certs.
[08:20] Tom: Marketplace listings typically use the marketplace's contract flow — that should be manageable; for special legal terms we'll coordinate with Redwood legal.
[08:29] Maya: One more networking nuance — we use Envoy as sidecar for some clusters, will that interact poorly with Redwood connectors?
[08:36] Priya: Not usually; connectors talk to the control plane over HTTP/TLS and can sit alongside Envoy. We'll give an example config.
[08:45] [09:12] Diego: For compliance we also need audit events forwarded to our SIEM. Can Redwood forward logs to a customer endpoint?
[09:19] Linus: Yes for private deployments we can forward audit logs over syslog/HTTPS webhooks to your SIEM, or we can push into a bucket you control. We'll document retention options.
[09:33] Rina: Retention default?
[09:35] Priya: Default is 90 days in hosted control plane; enterprise retention is configurable with add-on.
[09:43] [10:02] Sam: Okay sounds good. Let's talk timeline: We want listing live in about 5 weeks. Is that feasible?
[10:10] Jordan: That should be feasible. Steps: 1) exchange network artifacts this week, 2) agree on billing metering and legal scope, 3) run benchmark, 4) finalize listing package. If all goes well, 5 weeks is realistic.
[10:26] Maya: I'll share cluster CIDR and egress topology by Monday.
[10:29] Priya: We'll send the VPC peering template and outbound connector config by Wednesday.
[10:36] [11:05] Linus: Quick technical note: if you run quantized model locally you'll want to set KV cache limits and pre-allocate workspace otherwise you'll see OOMs on start. We'll include recommended runtime flags.
[11:18] Maya: Noted — we've seen some OOM during warmup on previous runtimes.
[11:23] Diego: On KMS integration, any audit token we can tie to our HSM hardware attestation?
[11:30] Linus: We can do an attestation flow; requires some client-side cert exchange and a short attestation handshake. We'll put a whitepaper link in the notes.
[11:40] [12:00] Jordan: Cool. Let's recap action items. Priya will draft networking templates; Maya will send cluster details; Jordan will send pricing and checklist; and Linus will share benchmark plan and runtime flags.
[12:14] Sam: Great, we'll review and get back. Thanks everyone.

End of call.
notes: Shared artifacts: (1) lighthouse-network-diagram-v1.pdf (customer uploaded), (2) redwood-marketplace-checklist-draft.docx (Redwood will share), (3) quant-profiles-v1.csv (Redwood SE). Links to be attached in CRM.
